title: Source transport for ordinary finite reduction
statement: Let C and C' be small categories with Grothendieck topologies J and J'. Let L : Sh(J) → Sh(J') have right adjoint V with adjunction adj : L ⊣ V and preserve finite limits, and let F : InverseImageData L be the supplied constant-coefficient algebraic inverse-image data. For every commutative Noetherian ring A, ideal I, and n : ℕ, the functor res(coefficientMap J A I) followed by pull F (constantMap F A) and change(quotient J' A I n) is naturally isomorphic to change(projection J A I n) followed by pull F (constantMap F (A / I^(n+1))).

lean.statement:
theorem ordinaryReducedPull_sourceIso
    (V : Sheaf J' (Type u) ⥤ Sheaf J (Type u)) (adj : L ⊣ V)
    [PreservesFiniteLimits L] (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (n : ℕ) :
    Nonempty ((res (coefficientMap J A I) ⋙ pull F (constantMap F A) ⋙
        change (quotient J' A I n)) ≅
      (change (projection J A I n) ⋙
        pull F (constantMap F (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)))))

statement_change.old_statement: For the constant-completion coefficient data, the source finite-reduced functor admits a natural isomorphism to the canonical finite quotient model change(projection J A I n) followed by pullback along constantMap F (A / I^(n+1)).
statement_change.what: Restore the geometric inverse-image hypotheses assumed by the source and by the parent ordinary reduced pull theorem. Section variables V, adj, and finite-limit preservation were not included in the old Lean theorem. Invariants from C2-sets to sets preserve finite limits, constant rings, and all algebraic operations, but do not preserve reduction: for A = ℤ, I = (2), n = 0, and the completed module ℤ₂ with sign action, the source is zero and the target is ℤ/2. Thus even finite-limit preservation alone does not imply the old assertion. An adjunction with L on the left supplies the geometric hypothesis in Stacks 03EL. The proof now uses exactly ordinaryFinitePull_existsUnique and finiteComparison as planned.
